# Psalm 85 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A)

---

**1** For the choir director. A psalm of the descendants of Korah. LORD, you showed such kindness to your land; you brought Jacob back from exile.

**2** You forgave your people's guilt; you buried all their sins. Selah

**3** You set aside all your fury; you turned away from your burning anger.

**4** Now restore us again, God of our salvation! Let go of your frustration with us.

**5** Are you going to be angry with us forever? Will your anger stretch on through every generation?

**6** Won't you bring us back to life again so your people can celebrate who you are?

**7** Show us your faithful love, LORD! Give us your salvation!

**8** I'm going to listen carefully to what God the LORD says — he's about to announce peace to his people, to those who are faithful. But they must not go back to their foolish ways.

**9** His salvation is so close for those who honor him! His glory is about to make its home in our land!

**10** Love and truth have run into each other; righteousness and peace have embraced.

**11** Truth grows up from the earth like a plant, and righteousness smiles down from heaven.

**12** The LORD will indeed pour out his blessings, and our land will produce an abundant harvest.

**13** Righteousness will march ahead of him, preparing the path for his arrival.

---
## PNEUMA's Meaning Notes

- **85:10-11**: This is pure poetry — love and truth running into each other's arms, righteousness and peace kissing! It's a vision of the world made right, where God's character qualities are no longer in tension but dance together.

- **85:12-13**: When God's righteousness and love are reconciled, even the ground responds with abundance. Spiritual restoration leads to material blessing — the whole creation participates.

— PNEUMA
